answer: Both, as first-class. zmx already serves both (attach for humans, run/send/tail/wait for agents), so zmux needs a human surface and a program surface, and neither may be an afterthought over the other.
body: zmx already serves both: humans attach, agents run/send/tail/wait. A TUI for a human and a control surface for an agent are different products with different fidelity demands (rendering a terminal vs modelling state truthfully). Which is primary, and is the other a supported secondary or out of scope?
title: Who drives zmux: a human at a keyboard, or an agent?
